top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice is a simple, general mechanism (cancelling the light shifts of the two clock states) that is analytically understood, reproduced at the 1e-18 level by independent laboratories, and credited cleanly to Katori (invention) and Ye (development to record accuracy and many-body clock physics). It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The citation should say invention and development and rest on demonstrated accuracy, not on promised applications. A mature, well-attributed prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with Katori or Ye, and only a shared Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson
